transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-01-13 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Megan Carter (Redwood AE), Javier Ruiz (Redwood SE), Anya Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Singh (Polaris Head of ML), Tom Becker (Infra), Laila Ahmed (Security), Evan (Data Ops)

[00:00] Megan Carter: Hey everyone, thanks for joining on a Tuesday, really appreciate you making time. Quick agenda — usage and cost forecast given your ramp, SLA expectations for Dedicated, and then — oncall and runbook so we don't scramble during launch. Does that sound right?
[00:10] Priya Singh: Yep that sounds good. We're, uh, excited to get more clarity on cost because the finance team is starting to push back a bit on token spend as we go to 1M DAU type numbers.
[00:18] Tom Becker: Also want to make sure burst behavior won't break our VPC peering rules, last time we saw unexpected egress.
[00:24] Javier Ruiz: Good call Tom. We'll walk through routing/fallbacks and also how caching and batching changes unit economics.
[00:30] Anya Patel: I'll capture action items as we go.
[00:33] 
[00:40] Priya Singh: Quick context — current usage profile is mostly inference for triage summaries and clinical note enrichment, about 120k requests per day, median sequence length ~220 tokens but tail up to 2k tokens for long notes. We expect a marketing-led growth push in Q2 that could increase traffic 3x.
[00:56] Evan - Data Ops: adding that about 30% of requests are deterministic reranking flows so caching could help there.
[01:03] Megan Carter: Great, so rough mental model: deterministic rerank + prefix caching gives you a good reduction in token costs. We'll put numbers in the cost spreadsheet. For Dedicated, you can also get predictable throughput which helps with SLA.
[01:15] Priya Singh: On SLAs — finance will only sign a commit if we can get at least 99.9% availability and clear incident accountability.
[01:22] Laila Ahmed: And security needs to see evidence of key management and audit logs — KMS, HSM integration, and SSO/SAML for RBAC.
[01:30] Megan Carter: Totally. We'll share our SOC2 artifacts and our private deployment KMS guide. Note: private and VPC options have customer-managed keys and audit integration.
[01:38] 
[01:45] Javier Ruiz: Quick technical aside — for your workload with the long tails, we recommend a hybrid approach: host the bulk of low-latency inference on Dedicated pools with an autoscale/burst policy, and route very long sequences to a higher-memory variant or a private deployment flavor to keep latency SLOs. That reduces queuing for short calls.
[02:05] Tom Becker: When you say "variant" — is that a quantized model or different architecture? We worry about hallucination regressions if the model changes.
[02:13] Javier Ruiz: Good point. Variant could be a quantized-compatible variant of the same model family. Redwood Optimize will flag quality regression thresholds — we can pin the exact weights for canary and fallback. We recommend doing A/B tests on a holdout set of clinical prompts first.
[02:30] Priya Singh: Can you also explain unit costs? Our last invoice was hard to deconstruct.
[02:35] Megan Carter: Sure. There are a few levers: raw per-token compute cost, caching hit-rate, batching efficiency, and committed discounts on Dedicated. I'll give an example: with 50% cache hit-rate and 8x batching, your effective per-1k-token price drops substantially compared to on-demand. We'll model scenarios in the spreadsheet.
[02:55] 
[03:01] Evan - Data Ops: Are there any hidden costs, like KV-cache storage or egress?
[03:05] Javier Ruiz: KV cache is included as part of the serving runtime — small charges for long-term persistent caching may apply if you exceed in-memory cache sizes. Egress is standard cloud egress; if you run Private on-prem, egress is a non-issue.
[03:18] 
[03:25] Laila Ahmed: About auditability — we need immutable audit logs for every inference request that touches PHI, plus key rotation policy. Do you offer WORM-style logs or integrations with our SIEM?
[03:36] Megan Carter: We support audit logging to your logging sink (e.g., Splunk, BigQuery). For Private we can enable KMS-managed wrapping and send logs to your SIEM. We'll include a security pack that outlines rotation policy and retention.
[03:50] 
[03:55] Priya Singh: I want to drill into the on-call playbook. Last time an incident occurred, our ML team couldn't find the right owner and response lagged. We're aiming for a clear escalation matrix.
[04:05] Anya Patel: We've prepped a runbook template that includes start-of-shift checks, playbook steps for latency spikes, how to toggle fallbacks (e.g., model downgrade to a simpler variant), and postmortem checklist. I'll send the template after the call.
[04:18] Tom Becker: Important: the runbook must include network troubleshooting steps because our infra folks will likely be first responders.
[04:25] Javier Ruiz: We'll add infra steps — checks for GPU saturation, network egress, queuing stats, and how to flip to a regional fallback. We'll also add the Redis/KV-cache eviction thresholds and what to do if prefix cache hits drop.
[04:40] 
[04:45] Priya Singh: Pilot timeline — ideally we start a 4-week pilot in March, with a week for baseline tests, two weeks for tuning and load ramp, and one week for handoff. Is that feasible?
[04:56] Megan Carter: Yes, March pilot window looks doable. We should lock in the baseline tests and size the Dedicated pool before the pilot. Javier, can you run a sizing sim?
[05:05] Javier Ruiz: Yep — I'll need sample traffic shape and token distribution to simulate batching and cost. Tom, can you share that CSV?
[05:11] Tom Becker: Yep I'll send it by Friday (2026-01-15).
[05:14] 
[05:20] [06:00] (brief silence while people reference shared deck)
[06:05] Priya Singh: I also want to bring up data residency — some PHI workflows need EU data residency. Do you have region pinning for Dedicated?
[06:13] Megan Carter: Yes, Dedicated pools can be regionally pinned. For Private we can deploy in your VPC in EU regions. We'll map options in the SOW.
[06:22] Laila Ahmed: Any notes on federation or hybrid key access? We can't have keys leave our HSM.
[06:28] Megan Carter: For Private, we support HSM-backed KMS where keys never leave your control. For hosted we offer KMS integration but the customer-managed key wrapper depends on the plan. We'll clarify in the security packet.
[06:40] 
[06:45] Javier Ruiz: I'd like to show a quick estimate — if we take your current 120k req/day with median 220 tokens and assume 30% caching, rounding — your projected monthly token consumption is about X million tokens and with a medium batching configuration you'll be at roughly $Y/month on Dedicated with a 12-month commitment — the exact numbers will be in the spreadsheet.
[07:08] Tom Becker: The finance team wants tiered pricing and a cap on cost growth during ramp. Can we see a pricing ladder?
[07:15] Megan Carter: Absolutely. We'll provide tiers and an overage policy. We can also propose a right-sizing clause after 90 days.
[07:22] 
[07:28] Priya Singh: On quality — if you suggest quantization to reduce cost, we need regression tests for hallucination rates on clinical prompts.
[07:36] Javier Ruiz: Agreed. We'll run evals on your prompt set and surface delta metrics. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization configs that minimize quality drift; but we will not suggest a change without the eval baseline.
[07:49] 
[08:00] Anya Patel: Action items recap — (1) Megan to share pricing and SOW; (2) Javier to run sizing sims once Tom shares traffic; (3) Anya to share runbook template; (4) Laila to send security questions to Redwood and Redwood to respond. Anything to add?
[08:13] Priya Singh: Please include an explicit rollback policy in the runbook — e.g., how to revert model weights or route traffic back to openai fallback if needed.
[08:22] Javier Ruiz: We do have automatic fallback policies — route by policy to an alternative model or region. We'll document the rollback steps and timing.
[08:30] Tom Becker: Also include expected latency distributions per model variant in the doc so we can set SLOs properly.
[08:36] Megan Carter: Will do.
[08:40] 
[08:45] [10:00] Cross talk: "yeah", "mmm", small interruptions as people agree
[10:12] Priya Singh: One more ask — can Redwood run a small reliability test to simulate node failures during the pilot so we can validate autop-scaling/failover behavior?
[10:22] Javier Ruiz: Yes we can do a controlled chaos run during the pilot. We'll schedule that in the tuning phase and work with Tom on safety gates.
[10:32] 
[10:35] Laila Ahmed: Security timeline — we'll need SOC2 and encryption docs by next Tuesday to start our review with compliance.
[10:42] Megan Carter: We'll bundle those and target 2026-01-20 delivery.
[10:47] 
[11:00] Anya Patel: Ok final recap and deadlines: pricing SOW by 2026-01-16 (Megan), traffic CSV by 2026-01-15 (Tom), runbook and oncall template by 2026-01-18 (Anya), security Q&A response by 2026-01-20 (Redwood). Pilot baseline to be scheduled for week of 2026-03-02 pending agreements.
[11:20] Evan - Data Ops: Sounds good to me.
[11:25] Priya Singh: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[11:28] Megan Carter: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the packet and the spreadsheet. I'll put the plan in the CRM and send calendar invites for the benchmark run.
[11:38] (meeting ends)

Notes/Links referenced: cost spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.co/sheets/polaris-cost-model), runbook template (link: https://redwood.co/docs/runbook-template), security pack placeholder (link: https://redwood.co/security/polaris-pack)

Transcript notes: automated transcript contains occasional mis-attribution and audio gaps around 05:20-06:00. Some acronyms transcribed oddly (K M S vs KMS, VPC as V-C-P, KV cache as KV cash in one line).
